prior_importants.description: The 'every side is a known binary' rule only reads `path` at the merge-base and at the branch. For a rename, `gitDiffNumstat` reports only the new path, so the rename's source file is never checked or counted. Renaming a source file into a `.png` therefore drops all its deleted lines, with no forged flag.

Test adequacy: no test fails if the new `--no-relative` in rawDiffEntries is removed. The new core.worktree + diff.relative test has no rename and no symlink with a test name, so an empty raw map changes no count.

findings.description: When `--numstat` reports a binary rename or mode-only change as `-\t-`, the old and new oids are the same. Two kinds of file now get flagged where they used to be skipped: a file outside the table (GIF, PDF, WOFF2, WebP), and a PNG over 1 MiB. The recount diffs the oid against itself, which gives `{0, 0}`, and `countChangedLines` still pushes it to `forged` because it only checks `!recount`. Known PNGs moved unchanged also spend the 4 MiB budget.
findings.body:
**An unchanged move of a binary is now filed as forged**

Git's numstat prints `-\t-` for a binary pair even when the content is unchanged. It sets `is_binary` before `same_contents` zeroes the counts. (This is pinned-version knowledge of git's `diff.c`, not a spike.) `gitDiffNumstat` forces `diff.renames=true`, so an exact rename (R100) of a binary reaches `gitDiffBinaryRecount` with `baseBlob.oid === branchBlob.oid`:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/6ed129a7446baf49cdea7503dc589aa5f0b5c01b/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L843-L855

What happens next:
- **A path outside `BINARY_FORMATS` (PDF, GIF, WOFF2, WebP):** `formatsNamed` returns `[]`, so `sides = [false]` and the skip is refused. `diffHunks(repo, [oid, oid])` returns no hunks, so the function returns `{ added: 0, deleted: 0 }`.
- **A PNG over `BINARY_FREE_MAX_BYTES`:** the skip is refused the same way.
- **The forged flag:** `countChangedLines` only checks `if (!recount) continue;`. `{0, 0}` is truthy, so the path goes into `forged`:

  https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/6ed129a7446baf49cdea7503dc589aa5f0b5c01b/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L698-L701

  That files a "Text files git reports as binary" debt entry and flags the diff-size stage, for a write that has nothing unread in it.
- **A known PNG under the cap moved unchanged:** it is skipped, but `spendKnownBinarySkip` charges its bytes to the 4 MiB budget. Moving an `assets/` directory of small PNGs therefore flags every file past 4 MiB.

**Trigger:** `git mv docs/manual.pdf docs/guide/manual.pdf` in any repo that commits a PDF. Before this PR, `blobIsBinary(branch, path)` found the NUL and skipped the file. ADR 0154's *Ceilings* accepts "one acceptance per merge that **adds** one", and a byte-identical move adds nothing. The existing test `skips a known binary renamed from a known binary` changes the content, so it doesn't cover this.

**Possible fix:** when both sides exist with the same oid and mode, nothing new entered the tree, so answer `null` before the budget is spent. That matches a text R100, which numstat counts as `0\t0`. Place it right after `const [baseBlob, branchBlob] = entry.sides;`:

```ts
if (baseBlob?.oid === branchBlob?.oid && baseBlob?.mode === branchBlob?.mode) return null;
```

`DiffSides` never has both sides undefined, so this only holds for two identical sides. A mode-only change (same oid, 100644 → 100755) is still recounted and flagged, which matches the ADR's rule for an executable PNG. A test would pin the move: commit a `.pdf` holding a NUL, `git mv` it, and assert nothing goes into `forged` and the budget is unchanged.

findings.description: The filesNaming JSDoc still says 'a listed path the tree does not hold refuses', but commit 4c2ab2a removed that throw: such a path is now read as naming every target (lines 586-591), like a U+FFFD name. A maintainer trusting the doc expects a refusal that no longer happens. Replace the clause with 'a listed path the tree does not hold names every target, as one not UTF-8 does' (ADR 0154 lines 135-137 already say so).

The ADR says the readBlobs batch runs under GIT_READ_TIMEOUT_MS (30 s) "as does the `ls-tree` behind each known-binary check". No ls-tree in the diff-size path takes that timeout: the known-binary check now sizes each side with `cat-file -s` (src/core/git-diff.client.ts:785), and that call carries the timeout. Someone auditing which calls are bounded under the merge lock would look for a timeout on an ls-tree that isn't there. Name `cat-file -s` instead.

`mayBeKnownBinary` is written as `!(size > BINARY_FREE_MAX_BYTES)` so that a NaN size passes, and its JSDoc justifies that with the `ls-tree` `BAD` size. Its only caller, `blobIsKnownBinary`, gets `size` from `blobSize` (`cat-file -s`), which throws on a bad object, so NaN never reaches it. Use `size <= BINARY_FREE_MAX_BYTES` and drop the NaN paragraph; that removes a double negation and a comment pointing a maintainer at the wrong path.

`spendKnownBinarySkip` mutates its argument (`budget.bytes -= spent`), but docs/conventions/naming.md says `utils` hold "pure functions only". A caller reading a utils module could pass a shared budget object without expecting it to be drained. Return the remaining budget, or move the function next to its caller in git-diff.client.ts, which owns the budget.

`blobIsKnownBinary` and `blobLines` each call `blobSize` (a `cat-file -s` process) and then `readBlobs(repoPath, [oneBlob])`, with the same `[blob = Buffer.alloc(0)] = readBlobs(...)` unwrapping written out twice. A small `readBlob(repoPath, oid)` next to `blobSize` would remove the duplicated unwrapping and the array wrapping at both sites.

refuted_findings.description: Under a `-diff` or `binary` attribute, a submodule path reads `-\t-` in numstat; its `--raw` sides are mode 160000 commit oids, so the recount runs `git diff <commit> <commit>` / `cat-file -s` / readBlobs on a commit and the gate errors on every such submodule bump.
refuted_findings.refutation: Git applies diff attributes only to regular files: `diff_filespec_load_driver` looks up the attribute driver only when `S_ISREG(mode)`, and a gitlink's populated content is the text `Subproject commit <oid>\n`, which has no NUL. Numstat therefore prints `1\t1` (or `1\t0`/`0\t1`) for a gitlink, never `-\t-`. merge-gate.service.ts:694-698 counts any entry with numeric counts directly, and gitDiffNumstat sets `sides` only for a `-` count, so gitDiffBinaryRecount is never reached for a submodule. Pre-PR behaviour was the same. (Medium confidence: rests on git's diff.c internals, not a spike.)

process_issues.description: The orchestrator's first review-correctness spawn went out with a placeholder brief (the literal text "BRIEF"), so that instance reviewed only the top commit 6ed129a. It found nothing. Two properly briefed correctness instances were then spawned, split into the numstat/recount/known-binary decision and the readBlobs/batched reach checks, so correctness ran as three instances. Only the two briefed instances covered the full PR.
